# AgentPROV v0.1 — Architecture decision brief (binding for spec writers)

Date: 2026-10-07. Author: principal architect (synthesis of `investigation/` reports).
Status: DRAFT-FOR-SPEC. Every spec section must be consistent with this brief; where a section writer
finds evidence that a decision is wrong, they must say so explicitly in a "Challenge" box rather than
silently diverge.

Evidence base: `audit/*.md` (5 code audits), `baseline/BASELINE.md`, `manuscript/*.md`,
`sources/*.md` + `verify/*.md` (12 sources, adversarially verified), `landscape/prov_semantics.md`,
`landscape/trace_formats.md`, `landscape/secure_ingestion.md`.

---

## D0. Central principle

AgentPROV is an **execution-provenance framework with benchmark/framework adapters**. The conceptual
centre is a *source-preserving, evidence-qualified canonical execution record*, not AgentDojo and not
a transcript. AgentDojo is one adapter family (live + import) and the regression baseline.

Pipeline (each arrow is a pure, versioned function except the first):

```
live backend (AgentDojo, AutoDojo)  ──►  RAW capture artefacts ─┐
released logs / corpora (import)    ──►  RAW source artefacts  ─┤  immutable, sha256-addressed, untrusted
                                                                 ▼
                        adapter.map(raw, adapter@ver, rules@ver)  ──►  AER   (canonical execution record)
                        semantics(AER, semantics-profile@ver)     ──►  SEM   (standoff annotations)
                        provenance(AER, SEM, prov-spec@ver)       ──►  PROV  (PROV-JSON w/ bundles; PROV-O TriG)
                        validate(...) gates every write; package(...) seals the corpus manifest
```

**Live capture produces raw evidence and is then mapped by exactly the same machinery as an import.**
There is one canonical model, one provenance engine and one validator for both modes.

## D1. Rejected: transcript/v2 as the core (previous plan)

A message list + extensions cannot represent: model calls separate from messages (discarded replies,
auxiliary/defence LLMs, what the model saw), tool executions separate from tool messages
(undispatched/denied calls, mutated args), defence decisions, fixtures (injection payloads, attack
plans), partial/unknown order, or evidence classes. It also perpetuates the core PROV defect the audit
found (one activity standing for both the LLM inference and the tool execution). A transcript view is
still produced (as a derived *view*), and transcript/v1 survives as an *import format*.

## D2. Canonical model: AER — AgentPROV Execution Record (`aer/0.1`)

Adopt the typed-record design of `landscape/trace_formats.md` §6 with these decisions:

- One execution = one JSONL file `<ex>.aer.jsonl`; each line one record in RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical
  form; first line `execution` header, last line `seal` (record count + sha256 over preceding lines =
  the **execution digest**).
- Record kinds (closed core vocabulary): `execution`, `actor`, `scope`, `message` (parts typed after
  OTel GenAI part types: text, reasoning, tool_call, tool_result, blob, file, uri, refusal, other),
  `model_call`, `tool_execution`, `decision`, `state_change`, `fixture`, `judgement`, `seal`.
- Envelope on every record: `k`, `id`, `ev` (O/D/I), `by` (capture|source|provider|benchmark|config|
  replay), `evf` (per-field evidence overrides, JSON Pointer keys), `rule` (versioned rule ids
  `<ns>.<rule>@<n>` for every D/I assertion), `src` (locators into raw artefacts: JSON Pointer,
  zip-member+pointer, byte range, line, git blob), `unk` (pointer → reason ∈ not_recorded | lost |
  withheld | ambiguous | not_captured | not_applicable), `after` (sparse happens-before edges with basis
  causal|time|pos|proto), `ext` (declared namespaces only).
- Core fields are closed (`additionalProperties: false`); framework data goes to `ext.<ns>`.
- **Sentinel values are forbidden** (no `"0"` timings, no `""` stand-ins); use `unk`.
- Ids: execution id for imports = `ex_` + base32(sha256("aer-ex/1\n" + adapter.id + "\n" +
  artefact.sha256 + "\n" + locator))[:26]; live = `ex_` + UUIDv7 recorded in the capture log. Local
  ids are positional (`m<n>`, `m<n>#<k>`, `mc<n>`, `te<n>`, …), never provider ids or content hashes.
- References are backward-only (single-pass streaming validation). Tool result ↔ call linking records
  how it was established (D: unique call-id match; I: positional; O: structural link in source).
- Absence of an `after` edge means order **unknown**, never concurrent. File line order is a
  serialisation order only.
- Large/binary content → content-addressed blobs in the raw store, referenced `{"$blob":"sha256:…"}`.
- A JSON Schema (`schemas/aer-0.1.schema.json`) is published for consumers; the in-code validator is
  authoritative and is differentially tested against the schema.

## D3. Raw evidence store (immutable, untrusted)

- Raw artefacts are stored byte-identical, addressed by sha256, with an origin record
  (git repo + commit + path + blob sha1 | HF dataset + revision | URL + retrieval date | live capture
  session). Upstream logs are fetched from **pinned commits / DOIs** (e.g. AgentDojo legacy logs from
  `ethz-spylab/agentdojo@c274885…:runs/`, or the Zenodo software deposits), never "latest".
- Live capture writes: (1) a hash-chained capture event log `capture/0.1` (session, wire LLM request
  and response incl. discarded/retried replies, tool dispatch + result, pass boundaries, env digests,
  instrumentation declaration), (2) the native AgentDojo TraceLogger JSON the stock harness would
  write. Both are raw evidence; (2) enables a live-vs-native differential test.
- Corpus releases either **include** raw artefacts (licence permits) or **reference** them (hash +
  fetch recipe) when redistribution is not permitted (e.g. CIAware-Bench: no licence; gated).

## D4. Adapter model = reader (dialect) + mapper + source profile

- **Reader/dialect**: safe parser for a physical format. v0.1 dialects: AgentDojo TraceLogger JSON
  (June-2024 11-key; 2025+ 14-key with `benchmark_version`/`evaluation_timestamp`/
  `agentdojo_package_version`; DRIFT-extended; AgentDyn variants), AgentDojo-PROV `transcript/v1`,
  AgentPROV `capture/0.1`, STAC JSON array (MultiTurnAgentAttack). Planned: Inspect AI `.eval`.
- **Mapper**: raw → AER, emitting versioned rule ids for every D/I assertion; declares unknowns.
- **Source profile** (data, not code, where possible; TOML/JSON shipped in the package): framework id,
  canonical repo, pinned commits, licence + redistribution policy, lineage/overlap, dialect(s), suite
  and task semantics, rule catalogue, quirks (e.g. ROPE system-prompt line; AgentDojo DoS polarity;
  benign `security` constant; 3-pass silent re-run), live/import capability, implementation status.
- **One AgentDojo-family importer** serves AgentDojo upstream, ROPE (incl. AutoDojo-attack runs),
  AgentDyn, DRIFT, Mandate-AgentDojo-Eval and the survey's own runs via profiles. AgentDojo-Inspect's
  runs are a byte-identical mirror of AgentDojo runs → no separate corpus (dedup by `source_key`).
- **Registry**: explicit in-repo registry (`agentprov.adapters.registry`), no entry-point plugin
  loading in v0.1 (supply-chain risk; no evidence third parties need it yet). Adding a framework =
  new reader/mapper module + profile + rule catalogue + tests; the provenance engine, AER schema,
  validator and corpus layer are untouched unless a genuinely new *record kind* is needed (then it is
  a versioned AER schema change — the future-framework test must show this is rare).

## D5. Live execution backends

- `ExecutionBackend` protocol: plan (cells) → execute → write raw capture artefacts → (shared) map →
  derive → validate → package. Generic capture session: per-pass accounting, generalised accounting
  gate (agent vs auxiliary LLM roles; tool dispatch ↔ result 1:1), env digests/diffs, atomic writes,
  resume from sealed raw evidence; **failing executions are sealed and kept with issues, never
  silently discarded** (selection effects must be measurable).
- **AgentDojo backend**: port of the baseline capture (`_CompatLLM` recording gateway,
  `TranscriptCapture`/`EnvironmentRecorder` pass recorder, `TimingToolsExecutor` behaviour-preserving
  mirror with a differential test against stock `ToolsExecutor`), now writing `capture/0.1` raw
  evidence. Pinned `agentdojo==0.1.35`. Remove the in-loop `ProvObserver` (second PROV implementation).
  Record every harness deviation (developer→system role rewrite, retries, resampling, temperature not
  transmitted) as declared instrumentation in the execution header (observer effects).
- **AutoDojo backend**: AutoDojo is an AgentDojo 0.1.35 fork with the *same distribution name and
  version*; it cannot share an environment with PyPI agentdojo. Run it in an **isolated uv
  environment** pinned to an inspected AutoDojo commit, via a worker subprocess that loads the same
  AgentPROV capture hooks and writes `capture/0.1`. Tests use a scripted fake LLM client (no network,
  no keys), following `tests/test_attempts.py`. Real model runs require the user's keys and consent.

## D6. Semantic layer: SEM (`sem/0.1`)

Standoff annotations over AER ids, produced by a versioned **semantics profile** supplied by the
adapter family (e.g. AgentDojo suite tool tables → integrity (three-valued: trusted/untrusted/unknown,
fail-closed for unknown tools), roles (sink/endorser/read/egress), source channel; injection-marker
algorithm with explicit format normaliser (YAML/repr) and error model; outcome interpretation with
explicit polarity). Every annotation carries evidence class + rule id. SEM is hashed separately.

## D7. Provenance engine and specification (`agentprov-prov/0.1`)

Adopt `landscape/prov_semantics.md` §4, §7.2, §8–§10:

- **Decomposed model**: `ModelInvocation` activities (use every as-sent context message, tool
  definitions, model entity; generate the assistant message and tool-call request entities);
  `ToolExecution` activities (use only their request [+ env state when captured]; generate tool-result
  entities); pass/run activities; environment state entities when captured; checker activities for
  outcomes; agents: agent system, model service, tool runtime (acting on behalf of the agent),
  simulated user, attacker, checker.
- **Bundles**: core bundle (OBSERVED + DERIVED PROV statements only); inference bundles (INFERRED PROV
  statements, one per method, attributed to the method); assessment bundle (non-PROV claims:
  integrity, roles, exposure, taint, injection marker — via `prov:mentionOf` entities and
  `apv:Assessment` entities, never as `prov:used`/`wasDerivedFrom`). Top level states the provenance
  of the conversion: raw → AER → bundles, `hadPrimarySource(bundle, raw)`, engine/adapter agents,
  rule catalogue as `prov:Plan`.
- **Evidence attributes** on every node and identified relation: `apv:evidenceClass`, `apv:rule`,
  `apv:sourcePointer` (into AER), `apv:assumption` (closed list), plus `apv:method`/`apv:confidence`
  for inferred. Qualification annotates; it cannot hedge (a qualified relation still asserts the
  unqualified one) — hence the bundles.
- **Never emit**: used/wasInformedBy from temporal adjacency; tool-execution usage of anything but its
  request/env; wasDerivedFrom from context membership; channel attribution of composite outputs;
  wasInfluencedBy as a hedge; any time not recorded in the source. Order is `apv:` attributes only.
- `wasInformedBy` only via PROV-CONSTRAINTS Inference 6 premises (R-COMM-1/2), with `apv:premise`.
- Scale option recorded per profile: `context_encoding = members` (default) | `collection`
  (delta-derived context collections for very long traces).
- **Compatibility profile `adprov-v2.3-compat`**: the baseline `build_prov` ported verbatim, run on a
  transcript/v1 *view regenerated from AER*; regression gate = byte-identical graphs for the frozen
  baseline (golden fixtures in CI; full 35,691 locally). This is a regression oracle and migration
  bridge, explicitly *not* the recommended semantics. A documented semantic-diff maps every v2.3
  relation to its agentprov-prov/0.1 counterpart (kept, reclassified, moved to assessment, dropped).
- Vocabulary: new versioned `apv:` ontology at `https://w3id.org/agentprov/ns#` (w3id registration
  prepared, not submitted without the user's consent); instance IRIs
  `https://w3id.org/agentprov/exec/<ex>#<local>` (collision-free across graphs). The `adprov:` IRI
  stays frozen for the compat profile.
- Serialisations: PROV-JSON (bundled; deterministic key order), PROV-O TriG (named graph per bundle),
  optional flattened core-only PROV-JSON for consumers that cannot read bundles.

## D8. Validation tiers (each gates writes where cheap)

1. Input/ingest safety (size, depth, encoding, archive/path rules) — before parsing.
2. AER validator (envelope, closed fields, backward references, kind-typed refs, locators resolve
   against digest-checked raw bytes, JCS, seal hash, accounting checks).
3. SEM validator (targets exist, rule ids declared).
4. PROV structural (generic PROV-JSON), per-bundle PROV-CONSTRAINTS subset (faithful constraints
   separated from time "flags"), serialisation fidelity (round-trip + library-independent
   completeness), optional SHACL; **profile rules** (shape invariants of a provenance spec) separate
   from generic checks; **evidence linkage**: every core statement's `apv:sourcePointer` resolves to
   the AER field that justifies it.
5. Corpus: manifest/digest chain raw→AER→SEM→PROV, checksums, duplicates (`source_key`), lineage.
6. Regression/differential: v1→AER→v1 round trip; compat byte-identity; live-vs-native mapping;
   old-vs-new package on samples.
7. Property-based (Hypothesis) and fuzz tests on readers, ids, ordering, derivation determinism.

Skipped checks never count as passed; release mode is strict.

## D9. Corpus, manifests, versioning, Zenodo

- One corpus per source (`corpus_id`), optional collection manifest over several corpora.
- Layout: `corpus.json` (manifest), `executions.jsonl` (index: ex id, source_key, logical key, facets,
  digests, paths, status/issues), `raw/` (included) or `raw/REFERENCES.json`, `aer/`, `sem/`,
  `prov/<spec>/`, `rules/` (shipped rule catalogues + profiles), `checksums.sha256`, `DATASHEET.md`,
  `LICENSES/`. Paths sharded by execution id; human facets live in the index.
- Separate version numbers: software `agentprov 0.1.0`; `aer/0.1`; `sem/0.1`; `capture/0.1`;
  `agentprov-prov/0.1` (spec + rule catalogue); `apv` ontology `0.1`; adapter semver per adapter;
  rule ids `@n`; corpus semver; benchmark/framework identity = observed commits/digests, never just
  version strings (AgentDyn and AutoDojo both call themselves `agentdojo 0.1.35`).
- Recompute = content-addressed derivation check: re-map raw → identical AER digests; re-derive →
  identical SEM/PROV digests; an intended change is a visible rule/spec version bump.
- Exported corpora never in Git; Zenodo release builder prepares deposit archives + metadata; a new
  AgentPROV concept DOI will be used; nothing is published without explicit instruction.

## D10. Package & repo shape (Python ≥3.12, uv, src layout, minimal core deps)

Core runtime deps: `prov`, `rdflib`, `rfc8785` (JCS). Extras: `agentdojo` (live backend + replay;
pins `agentdojo==0.1.35`), `analysis` (pandas, pyarrow, networkx, numpy), `render` (pydot), `shacl`
(pyshacl), `dev` (pytest, hypothesis, ruff, mypy/pyright, jsonschema). No benchmark import in core
modules (enforced by an import-boundary test).

## D12. Manuscript

New repo-less-for-now LaTeX project at `~/Desktop/PhD/Labs/3. AgentPROV paper`
(local git), evolved from `adprov_paper.tex` (cas-dc, natbib, macros-via-generator). Strongest
defensible contribution: a specified, versioned, evidence-qualified derivation from hash-pinned raw
evidence to W3C PROV, shown on ≥2 structurally different sources with per-source information loss
quantified; corpus secondary. The old manuscript stays pinned to framework 579a908 (no compatibility
shim needed). Figure pipeline generalised: data (manifest-verified) → stats (typed values with
evidence level) → render (deterministic) → macros/tables → LaTeX, with a keyed macro accessor and a
legacy alias layer.

## Addendum A (2026-10-07, after verifier re-runs and the secure-ingestion study) — binding

**A1. Interpreter and process split (supersedes the Python line of D10).**
Core `agentprov` requires **Python ≥ 3.14** (stdlib `compression.zstd` for Inspect `.eval` members, tar
`data` filter default, 2025–26 tarfile/zipfile CVE fixes; evidence: `landscape/secure_ingestion.md` §2).
Core is stdlib-only for parsing untrusted bytes. Archive ingestion warns and records the interpreter
version below 3.14.8 (the two 3.14.8-only fixes do not apply to extraction-free, declared-size-checked
ingestion; see A2). **Live backends are separate uv projects** (`backends/agentdojo/`,
`backends/autodojo/`, each with its own `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and Python 3.12 to match the
baseline 3.12.14), sharing a small stdlib(+`rfc8785`)-only capture package `agentprov_capture` that
writes `capture/0.1` raw evidence. Core never imports `agentdojo`; `agentprov run <backend>` spawns
the worker with `uv run --project backends/<backend> …` and then ingests its raw output like any import.

**A2. Store-first, extraction-free ingestion.** Archives are never extracted to the filesystem; members
are streamed, metadata-validated (regular members only; no encryption; methods {0, 8, 93}; NFC labels
with casefold collision keys; duplicate/overlap/offset checks; per-member/total/ratio/count limits) and
stored by sha256 in the content-addressed raw store. Member names are labels, never paths. Strict JSON
loader (byte cap, strict UTF-8, duplicate-key rejection, no NaN/Infinity/overflow, iterative depth cap
256); binary JSONL iteration with per-line caps and (line, byte offset) locators; bounded decompression.

**A3. Adapter isolation.** Import mapping runs in worker processes (spawn context; `python -I`;
minimal env; RLIMIT_CPU/FSIZE/NOFILE/CORE (+AS on Linux); RSS watchdog; wall timeout) — the same pool
gives deterministic parallel import. `--in-process` exists for debugging only and is recorded.

**A4. Secrets.** `.env` read only by the live CLI entry; header/parameter allowlist for recorded wire
requests (never `authorization`, api keys, `key=` query values); gitleaks pre-commit + release-tree scan;
a `WITHHELD.json` policy instead of editing raw evidence. All display of source text to humans or LLM
agents goes through `quote_untrusted` (escape controls, bidi, zero-width, tag chars; fenced with locator
and hash). Corpora and upstream clones live outside the repo working tree.

**A5. PROV catalogue corrections (prov_semantics §13).** Tool-call requests are *members* of the
assistant message (`hadMember`), not `wasQuotedFrom` it (Constraint 42 would claim strict precedence);
defence rewriting of a tool output is a separate defence activity (the later invocation is informed by
the defence, not the tool); structured-content author fields become declared-sender *attributes*, not
`wasAttributedTo`; checker activities use all of their inputs; re-run trigger content = null; one
mention per subject in the assessment bundle. Time-based checks are §6.2 "MAY flag" diagnostics, not
ordering-constraint violations; Constraint 24 is per (entity, activity).

**A6. Source status updates (verifier-corrected; amended 2026-10-08 by the architect under Addendum B:
R-62 accepted, RESOLUTIONS §2.2 B9 recorded).** Two columns from now on: *evidence availability*
and *AgentPROV implementation status*.
- **B9 (D11/A6/A7), recorded.** `spec/I_matrix.md` §I.1.1, as amended by RESOLUTIONS, replaces the D11 table
  and is the single source of v0.1 status values; the bullets below are rationale, not a second status table.
  Spec statuses are v0.1 targets: the registry downgrades any part whose gate fails, and `supported` requires
  a full pinned-snapshot import. Rows render per part or worst-case, never best-case.
- AgentDyn: variant A (38,281) supported; variants B/C partial. Variant C (4,258 files) consists of re-keyed
  and relocated copies of **AgentDyn's own** git-history blobs under `runs/DRIFT/<model>/…`, not of
  `SaFo-Lab/DRIFT` history → curation step recorded (`agentdyn.variant_c_rekey@1`); lineage edge E11 targets
  `agentdyn` · `history`, the owner is `agentdyn`, and DRIFT owns only the byte copies E09/E10 (R-62).
  Directory names are publisher-asserted labels; history-only executions (~11,297 novel) planned with
  fingerprint dedup.
- CIAware-Bench: partial evidence — public ungated Inspect `.eval` traces exist
  (`ciaware-anonymous-account/ciaware-traces`, no licence → reference-only; `superkaiba1/ciabench-
  trajectories`, MIT in card); GitHub records are truncated display strings. Implementation: via the
  Inspect importer (v0.1 target, see A7).
- Agent Security Tools Survey: discovery source AND execution source (CC-BY-4.0). Pin (R-62): primary
  origin git `Forever-CodingNoob/agent-security-tools-survey@89c4db2c949797fbb38c5bfed85dc82780ddbfe3`;
  alternative origins Zenodo v1.0.0 `10.5281/zenodo.22135957` and v1.0.1 `10.5281/zenodo.22140262`
  (archive contents not compared, so every member is verified by sha256); citations give the concept DOI
  `10.5281/zenodo.22135956` together with the version fetched. Contents: 3,243 AgentDojo runs (supported
  via TraceLogger importer; 2,385 outputs are Python repr, not YAML → marker normaliser registry),
  AgentHarm Inspect logs (Inspect importer), ASB (partial).
- MultiTurnAgentAttack (STAC): **scenario records, not executions** (scripted prefixes, real env outputs,
  1 partial real trajectory; no outcomes; CC BY-NC). Implementation: planned (stress test for scripted
  actors and code-derived ordering; array order is NOT generation order).
- ADI: not possible (no executions); live would need ADI's own fork in an isolated env.
- MiDojo: not possible. AgentDojo-Inspect: mirror of AgentDojo runs (no distinct corpus).
- AgentDojo upstream: cite the GitHub–Zenodo software deposits (concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.12528188)
  as immutable raw anchors; baseline legacy logs = upstream @ c274885 / Zenodo v0.1.7–0.1.8 subtree.
- AutoDojo: AgentDojo fork named `agentdojo 0.1.35` (hatchling); attack `autodojo` replays cached
  optimised injections (`AUTODOJO_CACHE`); inspected commit `aa458794b7eb7f082e94daeac4c0f55bfc0c90cc`.
  Released AutoDojo-attack executions live in ROPE; keep `security_raw` vs ROPE-corrected separate.

**A7. v0.1 importer order.** (1) adprov transcript/v1 (+ compat oracle); (2) AgentDojo TraceLogger
family (upstream, ROPE/AutoDojo, AgentDyn A, DRIFT, Mandate, survey runs); (3) capture/0.1 (live);
(4) **Inspect `.eval`** — first non-AgentDojo-lineage importer (survey AgentHarm logs CC-BY-4.0; CIABench
sample) — this is what licenses any "benchmark-agnostic" claim; (5) STAC scenarios (stretch).

## Addendum B (2026-10-07, architect rulings on spec/review/RESOLUTIONS.md) — binding, overrides A and the main text

The consolidated review (64 findings: 7 blocking, 40 major, 17 minor) and its 22 architect decisions
(AD-01…AD-22) are ruled as follows. "Accept" means the RESOLUTIONS.md recommendation is adopted verbatim,
including its canonical naming table (§3), which ALL sections must follow.

| AD | Ruling |
|---|---|
| AD-01 process split | **Accept.** `capture/` → `agentprov-capture` (≥3.12, stdlib + rfc8785); `backends/shared/` → `agentprov-backend`; backend projects never install `agentprov`; live runs exec `<env>/bin/python -I -B -m agentprov_backend.worker` with envs under `$AGENTPROV_HOME/envs/`; `live` extra with python-dotenv ≥1.2.2; `ScriptedTransport` in `agentprov_backend.testing`. |
| AD-02 lexical form | **Accept** C's sparse `ext.lex` via `aer.canon.lex_hints()`; views read nothing from raw; gates compare JCS and bytes, never Python `==`. |
| AD-03 aer/0.1 freeze table | **Accept**, plus B-1 below. |
| AD-04 execution id | **Accept** (`[0:26]`, mapping id `<adapter>/<profile>`, locator canon, KAT `ex_7uz2oys57hugtsueixylme4fl5`). |
| AD-05 evidence classes | **Accept** (static at map time; adapter-declared assumptions with identity-matched verification; released v1 context membership is INFERRED → inference bundle; native rows verified per code range or INFERRED). |
| AD-06 Inspect | **Accept**: normative Inspect importer in v0.1 and, with TraceLogger, the aer/0.1 + capture/0.1 freeze gate. |
| AD-07 migration gates | **Accept (c).** |
| AD-08 claims | **Accept with nuance:** "benchmark-agnostic" may describe the *architectural design goal* of the core (README/AGENTS/paper design sections); every *empirical* claim of coverage uses the registry-generated phrase ("adapter-based core; demonstrated on N sources in K formats (…)"), and only after the Inspect DoD item passes. "Live Capture" in a title needs an approved, sealed, non-test live corpus. |
| AD-09 live LLM element | **Accept**: stock LLM element + recording transport by default; `gateway_compat` (the `_CompatLLM` port) opt-in and declared as instrumentation. |
| AD-10 scope | **Accept with deviation:** keep (i) a minimal, generic `agentprov stats` (counts per source/status; PROV statements by evidence class/bundle/rule; unknown-reason proportions; per-source information-loss table — needed by the paper) in `src/agentprov/stats/`, and (ii) `agentprov render` — the baseline `visualize.render_prov_graph` ported to read agentprov-prov/0.1 bundles (core only by default), optional `render` extra (pydot + graphviz). All other AD-10 deferrals accepted (ML export, flow/argument baselines, replay, AgentDojo-specific analysis frames, TriG-per-execution storage, collections, fingerprints, etc.). The frozen baseline remains the home of the deferred analyses until ported. |
| AD-11 attack ground truth | **Accept (A)**: core bundle as configuration provenance. |
| AD-12 archive members | **Accept (a)**. |
| AD-13 live tier containment | **Accept (a) everywhere + (b) for real-model runs.** |
| AD-14 catalogues on rederive | **Accept (a)**. |
| AD-15 extensibility envelope | **Deviation — adopt a minimal (A):** aer/0.1 adds two generic record kinds, `activity` (fields: `type` = namespaced `<ns>:<name>`, `actor`, `scope`, `inputs` [backward refs to entity-like records], `t`, `status`, `label`) and `artefact` (fields: `type` = `<ns>:<name>`, `content` \| `content_ref` (`$blob`), `sha256`, `media`, `generated_by` [backward ref to activity \| model_call \| tool_execution]). EF adds generic rules G-ACT (typed prov:Activity), G-USE (used per input; class = evf of the input link), G-GEN (wasGeneratedBy from `artefact.generated_by`), G-ASSOC, and they participate in the Inference-6 closure. Rationale: requirement §10/§57 (new event types without core change) is an explicit acceptance criterion; with only `ext`, unseen non-LLM activities (memory reads, retrieval, code execution outside tool calls, browser actions) would produce no PROV at all. Specialised kinds remain preferred whenever they fit; adapters MUST NOT use `activity` for something an existing kind represents. Keep `other+subtype` escapes on the five enums. The D.12 / Q.3 future-framework test must produce named PROV statements for the planner step, memory write/read, screenshot, hand-off and human approval. |
| AD-16 interpreter | **Deviation — (c):** `requires-python = ">=3.14"`, `.python-version` `3.14`; archive/compressed-stream ingestion **refuses below 3.14.8 in release mode** (`--release`, `package`, `release`), warns and records `python_version` + `interpreter_advisory` in dev mode; CI pins the latest 3.14 patch. Reason: local uv 0.12.18 cannot install 3.14.8; development must not block. Recommend the user upgrades uv (≥0.12.22). |
| AD-17 PyYAML | **Accept** (core dep via `ingest/yamlsafe.py` only). |
| AD-18 profile/catalogue versions | **Accept** monotonic integers. |
| AD-19 PROV wording | **Accept** (hadMember with the message as prov:Collection; PROV-LINKS-correct mention wording; full Inference-6 closure over named activities; EF Ch1 (c)(e)(f)). |
| AD-20 layout + licence grouping | **Accept** both. |
| AD-21 CIAware | **Accept (a)** conservative. |
| AD-22 name | **Keep "AER"** (always expanded "AgentPROV Execution Record"; cite and distinguish Vispute & Kadam). Forwarded to the user (U-15) for a final say before the phase-6 freeze. |

**B-1 (record kinds).** aer/0.1 therefore has 13 kinds: execution, actor, scope, message, model_call,
tool_execution, decision, state_change, fixture, judgement, activity, artefact, seal.

**B-2 (user decisions).** U-01…U-18 of RESOLUTIONS §2.3 are forwarded to the user. Defaults applied until
the user says otherwise: no Zenodo deposit; no w3id submission (files prepared only); fixtures with
third-party model outputs only in the private repository and never in the sdist; MIT code licence with
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md; tags stay local; large downloads (Zenodo zips) only with consent — implement
fetch recipes and test on the samples already obtained; real-model live runs only with the user's
keys and consent; `upstream/` clones moved out of the session working directory (U-08, done by the
architect as a protective step).

**B-3 (spec location).** The final specification is published as `docs/architecture/` in the new repo:
`README.md` (index, executive architecture, decision record A + B) and one file per section.
